name: Beatrice Su
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember a customer asking if I could wait by his sleeping baby's room.” On Saturday, near Harbour Bakery, Beatrice buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I used to buy from the boy's dad. I'm offering childcare and he has good reason to check on me first.
appearance: Beatrice has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Beatrice folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Beatrice is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To offer childcare on terms the family can check.
family: Lark Kane is Beatrice’s younger cousin. Beatrice can always ask for five minutes alone. Lark asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Ten fingers*, Lark says, “I picked a green that flashes under stage light because I watch hands for a living.”
connections: Jade Hunter. A former customer offering childcare can be asked for references by the prospective foster aunt.

reactions.situation: His younger brother asks what he delivers for a living
reactions.response: Beatrice lets the older brother choose honest words the younger boy can understand.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Beatrice asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
